Proportional representation more or less instantly fixes most problems with democracies. It's pretty simple. A state is perfectly split up with 40% democrat, 35% republican, 25% libertarian. They have 100 representatives. What parties should their representatives come from? Most of everybody would agree with proportional representation where you get 40 democrats, 35 republicans, and 25 libertarians. What happens in first past the post? You get 100 democrats. To make first past the post work we split the state into 100 districts and each district has an election for a single winner-take-all seat. The first district votes 40% democrat, 35% republican, 25% libertarian - democrat gets the seat. Repeat 99 more times. It's idiotic and the reason even though fewer people than ever actually identify as republican or democrat, we get very near 100% of all government seats at all levels filled by democrats or republicans.

Even in things where there is only one seat this makes way more sense. Imagine if the electoral college was proportional. So if a state has 100 electoral votes and one candidate gets 55% and the other gets 45% then they get 55 and 45 votes respectively, instead of 100-0 as we currently have. Suddenly now every state matters instead of having a handful of "swing" states be the only ones the candidates care about.

It's sad really. First past the post is the source of most of our political alienation. And politicians are well aware of this, but it heavily benefits both sides of the political spectrum and so nobody talks about - and most citizens have no idea how bad first-past-the-post actually is since it sounds very fair until you study it to some degree.
